newsitem.title: USA: Conoco says upstream sales improve in Q2.
newsitem.headline: Conoco says upstream sales improve in Q2.

text.p: Conoco, an oil subsidiary of the DuPont Corp, reported an improvement in its second quarter upstream sales, however downstream operations fell short of last year's second quarter revenues.

Conoco said upstream sales, or sales from its drilling and exploration businesses, in the second quarter rose 3 percent to $1.06 billion. Downstream sales, or sales from its refining and consumer level businesses, slipped to $3.8 billion, a drop of 3.3 percent.

Commenting on this quarter's results, Archie Dunham, the president and chief executive officer of Conoco said, "the downstream improvement in the second quarter was driven by higher higher refined product margins and production from the new Lake Charles, La. lube hydrocracker facility."
Dunham added, "Upstream continued to perform well despite the decline in crude oil prices."
Conoco said in a statement that improvement in downstream operations were seen particularly in the U.S. Also contributing to the strong results were higher international gas sales.
Conoco reported a 39 percent increase in second quarter net income to $246 million.
